title: Signed FK percolation in Ising spin glasses
authors: Alberto Gandolfi, Charles Newman, Danile Stein
abstract: We introduce signed Fortuin-Kasteleyn (FK) percolation for the +/-J random-interaction Ising model to characterize nonzero uniform magnetization density and two-replica overlap within the class of Gibbs distributions whose infinite-volume Edwards-Sokal (ES)/FK representation has at most one infinite FK cluster almost surely. The construction refines ordinary FK connectivity by retaining the parity of coupling products along open paths. Using the infinite-volume ES representation and its DLR equations, we study pairs of companion objects and the compatible spin assignments on them. In one replica, companions are defined by positive-parity FK connections. For extremal states satisfying the infinite-cluster assumption and almost-sure existence of companion densities along the chosen van Hove sequence, nonzero limiting expected magnetization density is equivalent to density distinguishability of the companions of the infinite FK cluster. For two independent replicas, companions are defined by FK connections coherent in parity. For products of extremal one-replica states satisfying the infinite-cluster assumption and almost-sure existence of the companion densities along the chosen sequence, density distinguishability of the companions is equivalent to nonzero limiting expected mutual overlap. For two independent replicas drawn from the same extremal state, this specializes to the Edwards-Anderson self-overlap.
summary: This theoretical work develops signed Fortuin-Kasteleyn percolation to characterize order parameters in the random-interaction Ising spin glass. It proves that nonzero magnetization and mutual overlap are mathematically equivalent to specific density imbalances within the associated FK cluster companions. The methodology relies heavily on the Edwards-Sokal representation and advanced ergodic theorems for disordered systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to characterize two key order parameters in the $\pm J$ random-interaction Ising model: the nonzero uniform magnetization density and the two-replica mutual overlap.
main_result: It establishes mathematical equivalences between the existence of these non-zero order parameters and the density distinguishability of companion objects derived from signed Fortuin-Kasteleyn (FK) percolation clusters.
method: The analysis employs the infinite-volume Edwards–Sokal (ES) joint spin–FK representation, extending connectivity definitions to incorporate the parity of coupling products along open paths (signed FK percolation).
model_or_system: The system is the $\pm J$ random-interaction Ising model defined on an infinite graph ($\mathbb{Z}^d$), analyzed using techniques from statistical mechanics related to extremal Gibbs states.
key_observables: Nonzero limiting expected uniform magnetization density, two-replica mutual overlap, and the density distinguishability of FK cluster companions.
important_parameters: The coupling signs ($\pm J$), the temperature/inverse temperature ($ eta$), and the structure of the random couplings ($J$).
main_assumptions: The analysis critically assumes the existence of at most one infinite FK cluster almost surely, and the almost-sure existence of companion densities along a chosen van Hove sequence.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first defining signed FK percolation for single replicas (magnetization) and then extending the framework to two independent replicas (mutual overlap), culminating in rigorous theorems linking these physical quantities to companion density properties.
why_interesting: While focused on classical spin glasses, the rigorous mathematical machinery involving percolation, extremal states, and density convergence is highly relevant to understanding phase transitions and order parameters in complex quantum many-body systems.
